correctness.rationale: For the canonical centrally symmetric generator set, pairing opposite generators gives \(Z=\sum_{\alpha\in R_+}[-\alpha,\alpha]\) and hence the exact support function \(h_Z(u)=\sum_{\alpha\in R_+}|\langle u,\alpha\rangle|\). Central symmetry proves that the inradius is the minimum of this support function on the unit sphere. Weyl invariance reduces the minimum to one chamber, where the support function is linear with coefficient \(s\); simplicial-cone geometry shows the minimum is attained exactly on minimizing chamber rays. The semistar sum \(s\) is a vertex, vertex-transitivity places every vertex on the same centered sphere, and the antipodal pair \(s,-s\) gives the matching lower bound for the circumradius. The proof handles reducible and unequal-root-length cases and does not assume uniqueness of the incenter.

value.rationale: The result gives two basic Euclidean invariants and the exact tangent facet-orbit set for the entire class of vertex-transitive zonotopes, a class already known to admit a complete structural classification but not a metric one in the inspected source. It reduces a continuous optimization over all sphere directions to the finitely many fundamental chamber rays and works uniformly for irreducible, reducible, equal-root-length, and two-root-length families. This is a structural metric lemma for a natural classified family, not a parameter substitution or finite-table recomputation.
